Dull pain in both temples; better pressure,

Belching of large quantities of offensive

PROLONGED, PERIODICAL FITS OF RAPID, INCESSANT, DEEP BARKING OR
CHOKING COUGH; as if from abdomen; taking away the breath; compel holding the sides
and ending in retching, vomiting (first of ingesta, then of mucus), nosebleed or cold sweat;
followed by loquacity. Typical whooping cough. Tickling like a feather or crumb in larynx.
